column2: A Town Is Born

Pilgrims, pedlars and stonemasons have followed the roads to the [target_wonder.GetName] for fifty years, and now some of them will not leave. Tents have become huts, the huts have become houses with tile roofs, and a market is held under the walls every Wellentag. The reeve of [target_province.GetName] asks whether this new town may stand.
Let them stay. [target_province.GetName] grows with them.
Burn the huts and take their goods. The wonder needs no hangers-on.
[target_wonder.GetName]

My scribes have all but moved into the [target_wonder.GetName]. They come back with ink to their elbows and armfuls of copied passages, old maps and the sayings of sages long dead, and the pages they lay before me tonight are better than anything they wrote before.
Let them read everything on its shelves.
Your scribes work in the [target_wonder.GetName], and your book will be the finer for it.
The Fountain of Youth

The fountain at the heart of the [target_wonder.GetName] is fed by a spring the gardeners swear has never run dry. I kneel at its rim and lower a silver cup into the water. It is cold enough to hurt my teeth, and as I drink, a warmth spreads from my chest to my fingertips. When I rise my knees do not ache. For the first time in years they do not ache.

The fountain is laughing at me. I can hear it! So I laugh back and leap in, clothes and all, and I swallow the water by the mouthful until I choke on it. The gardeners drag me out by my collar. My bones creak, my eyes are dim, and my reflection in the pool is an old [Root.GetManWoman]'s face. The fountain has stopped laughing. I have not.
The years fall away.
I have never felt so old!
An Evening at the Tavern

Lamplight and loud voices spill from the tavern in the shadow of the [target_wonder.GetName]. [drinking_buddy.GetTitledFirstName] takes me by the arm. "You have the face of a [Root.GetManWoman] who has read too many tax rolls. One night, my friend. The ale here is brewed by the monks of the wonder and it would be a sin to let it go to waste."
Lead the way, and keep the cups coming!
Some who drink here never quite stop...
One cup, and then I would rather we talked.
One More Round

Since that first night I have gone back to the tavern by the [target_wonder.GetName] more often than I like to admit. The innkeeper knows my cup, the minstrel knows my favourite song, and my servants have learned to fetch me home before dawn.
Pour me another!
Deadly Traps

Curiosity has always killed more courtiers than the plague. [target_courtier.GetTitledName] and [target_courtier_2.GetTitledName] went into the deep vaults of the [target_wonder.GetName] with a lantern and a map they bought from a grave robber. The stones closed behind them. When the masons broke through two days later they found what the blades and the pit had left. [old_owner.GetTitledFirstName] built well.
Curse you, [old_owner.GetFirstName]!

Word comes from my old [target_wonder.GetName]: the traps I had laid in its depths still bite. [target_courtier.GetTitledName] and [target_courtier_2.GetTitledName] of [FROM.GetTitledFirstName]'s court went looking for my treasures and found my blades instead.
Ha! Let them enjoy their prize.

[target_vassal.GetTitledName],

The [target_wonder.GetName] is spoken of in every hall of my realm, and travellers who come to my court ask to see it before they ask to see me. You have kept it well. I wanted you to know that I have noticed.

[target_liege.GetTitledFirstName]
It is all thanks to my liege's guidance.
I have done well, haven't I?

My liege,

The [target_wonder.GetName] brings pilgrims, trade and glory to my lands, and I have never forgotten that I hold it under your protection. Thank you for your kind words.

[target_vassal.GetTitledFirstName]
A loyal vassal is worth a wonder.
Crumbling Stone

A carved stone the size of an ox has fallen from the [target_wonder.GetName] and smashed into the square below, missing a goose girl by a hand's breadth. The master mason says the mortar is a century old and tired, and that there will be more where that came from unless the scaffolds go up.
Raise the scaffolds. It will stand another hundred years.
Collectors will pay well for pieces of the [target_wonder.GetName]...
A Harvest from [target_province.GetName]

The keepers of the [target_wonder.GetName] send word that their stores are full. The gardeners have cut rare herbs from the beds, and the miners have brought up ore from the deep shafts that no smith in the province can name.
I will take the herbs.
I will take the ore.
